summary: Resolved the first-batch bootstrap cycle in the architecture plan: an explicit authorization-only October Web composition validates a real grant without opening an October database; generator prepare then verifies and migrates the owned empty target and creates the first batch; selected-data modes require the exact existing batch. Independent review and approval reconciliation remain root-owned.
finding_disposition: The accepted plan's first-batch dependency is no longer circular. Bootstrap Web needs only existing ordinary Identity/Data Protection and management authorization reads plus deployment-owned target/certificate allowlists; it exposes only the two closed grant/validation routes and cannot reach October data. Generator prepare uses that live authority, performs a read-only connected-target identity check before the sole authorized October migration, and commits first-batch setup atomically. Generator select and selected-data Web then bind an exact existing batch; neither may migrate or fall back.
feasibility: The ordinary Identity and management source of operator/Repository/context authority exists independently of an October database. The existing protected grant and mutual-TLS route contracts can therefore validate the first request before any October schema exists. The generator can connect to a specifically authorized empty PostgreSQL target for identity verification and migration without invoking a selector that requires a pre-existing batch.
invariants: Default ordinary Web remains without October routes/context/migration. Bootstrap mode has no October connection, selector, source approval or selected-data service; failed authority leaves the empty target unmigrated. Generator prepare never uses a preseeded batch, fake subject, cached allow, caller connection string or alternate target. If a later migration/setup step fails, no selectable partial batch is published. Selected-data modes reject missing/mismatched target and batch before downstream access.
migration_and_compatibility: Only generator prepare, after live authorization and connected target identity verification, applies the fixed October migration set to an explicitly owned target. Bootstrap and selected-data Web retain ordinary Identity/domain startup and never apply October migrations. October model/history stay separate; normal Web startup behavior remains unchanged. No JDT-LS, CodeGraph, Scan/Worker dispatch or Knowledge generation is added.
test_seam: The revised ID-T02 and quickstart require a fresh runner-owned empty PostgreSQL target: start bootstrap Web first, prove zero October connection/migration/selected-data route, obtain a real grant, run generator prepare to create the first batch, then start selected-data Web and generator select. Negative forged/missing grant cases must leave another fresh target empty; A/B mismatch and ordinary-startup regression remain. External database/certificate/runtime resources require separate explicit authority.
implementation_design_shape: Architecture classification, one document-level front matter block, exact headings and all existing design IDs are retained. No new design ID is needed because ID-R02/I02/I05/I06/S03/T01/T02/L02/C02 now express the bootstrap distinction. The installed plan-content validator returned no errors; git diff --check passed. Root owns authoritative path/hash-bound workflow validation after mapping.
authority_and_gate: Implementation approval remains withheld. The bootstrap correction changes the previously reviewed architecture boundary; the root must reconcile affected tasks, repeat independent review, and evaluate whether prior planned-change authorization remains applicable to corrected semantic scope. This self-review grants no approval or resource permission and does not alter the active recovery count or pause limit.
